text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp said Monday it supported consolidation in the aerospace industry.
Lockheed's statement came the day after Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp announced a merger plan valued at over $13 billion.

Lockheed said in a statement, "Given the precipitous -- and apparently continuing -- decline in the defense budget, further consolidation is necessary if we are going to maintain a viable defense industrial base in America at all."
Lockheed, a U.S. military contractor, said the proposed Boeing-McDonnell merger was another major step in continuing aerospace industry consolidation and it wished both companies well.
"From Lockheed Martin's perspective, we have always said our goal is not to be the biggest but the best," it said. "We are comfortable being a $30-billion 'David.'"
The Pentagon has chosen Lockheed and Boeing to build the U.S. military's 21st century joint strike fighter plane.
